speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To begin my evaluation, have you experienced any changes in bowel habits, urinary frequency, or abdominal bloating that feels like a persistent sensation of fullness?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the shortness of breath and abdominal girth, are you currently experiencing any difficulty breathing when lying flat (orthopnea) or waking up at night feeling short of breath (paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea)?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient denies orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, but reports significant fatigue alongside her shortness of breath and abdominal girth. Given the presence of a large ovarian mass and respiratory symptoms without heart failure signs, I am concerned about a massive pelvic tumor causing mass effect or potential metastasis. REQUEST TEST: CA-125. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis_With_Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CA-125: Normal; CT Abdomen/Pelvis With Chest: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites, right-sided pleural effusion.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or lower extremity swelling, and has no bowel or urinary changes. Given the large ovarian mass, shortness of breath, and fatigue without signs of heart failure or infection, I am concerned about a malignant ovarian neoplasm causing mass effect or pleural metastasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with likely malignant ascites and pleural effusion.
